thread:
sara.support: FYI — acme-prod reported intermittent 503s when calling our private API. They are in eu-west-1, hitting our private endpoint which should route to us-east-1. Logs show TLS hostname mismatch + connection reset. Need triage ASAP.

devon-sre: Can you paste the customer's curl/dig output and the exact error? Also which VPC peering (eu-west -> us-east) are they using?

sara.support: Peering ID pcx-0a1b2c3d. From customer host:

```
$ dig api.internal.redwood +short
10.12.45.21
```

```
$ curl -v https://api.internal.redwood/health
* TLS 1.2 connection to 10.12.45.21:443
* server certificate verification FAILED
* certificate: /CN=redwood-us-east.internal
* subjectAltName: host "api.internal.redwood" matched cert? NO
* Closing connection 0
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
```

sara.support: But from our control plane in us-east-1 dig shows: 

```
$ dig api.internal.redwood @10.0.0.53 +short
10.0.8.33
```

sara.support: So same name but resolving to different private IPs depending on region. Customer says when they resolve 10.12.45.21 requests fail (TLS CN mismatch), when resolved to 10.0.8.33 it works.

liam-net: This looks like split-horizon / region-local internal DNS returning local ENI IPs. If the customer's VPC peering doesn't have routes for those specific subnet ranges or SGs block traffic, packets may hit the wrong backend or a NAT device that presents a different cert.

ingress-bot: ALERT: tls_handshake_failures spike 2026-03-16T18:02:12Z -> topics: customer:acme-prod, route:private-api, reason:CN_MISMATCH

devon-sre: Can we get a traceroute from the customer to the failing IP and a packet capture of the TLS handshake? Also triage whether our LB is rewriting SNI or if a transit gateway/NAT is in the path.

sara.support: Traceroute (from acme host to 10.12.45.21):

```
traceroute to 10.12.45.21 (10.12.45.21), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.24 ms 0.19 ms 0.22 ms
 2  10.100.0.5  2.01 ms 1.99 ms 2.10 ms
 3  * * *
 4  192.168.200.1  12.03 ms 11.95 ms 11.88 ms
 5  10.12.45.21  12.10 ms 12.08 ms 12.06 ms
```

sara.support: tcpdump shows RST after TLS ClientHello. No server hello.

liam-net: Two likely root causes: 1) Cross-region peering returns an IP that terminates on a different internal LB with a cert not including api.internal.redwood; 2) Customer-side firewall/NAT is DNATing to an internal IP that we don't own so cert mismatch. Check peering route tables + our internal LB target-group registrations by IP.

marta-ops: Asked customer to run `dig +trace api.internal.redwood` and to query our internal resolver vs public. Also asked them to try `curl --resolve api.internal.redwood:443:10.0.8.33 https://api.internal.redwood/health` to see if forcing the 'working' IP succeeds. They reported forced curl returned 200.

devon-sre: Good repro. That proves DNS mapping to 10.12.45.21 is the failure vector. Next: confirm which service reports that IP in our control plane (maybe stale ENI or decommissioned host). Running `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=private-ip-address,Values=10.12.45.21` against customer account would help, but don't do that without their consent.

liam-net: I'm checking the internal LB config — seems we have per-region A records that point to local targets. We recently rolled a change that shortened TTLs, but some caches still have older mappings. Also noticed a route table entry in the customer's peering that only includes a /24 subset; 10.12.45.0/24 isn't in the advertised routes -> traffic may be sent to transit gateway instead.

devon-sre: For mitigation: 1) Tell customer to add 10.0.8.0/24 to their peering route (temporary). 2) We can add a SAN for the alternative cert/IPs or enable our region-fallback routing policy for this tenant so DNS returns the reachable region IP. Which is faster?

liam-net: Short term, customer route update is fastest. We'll also gate a config to include region aliases in the cert SAN list for internal endpoints (needs infra review).

sara.support: Customer applied route update (added 10.0.8.0/24 to peering). They see 200s now. Confirming stability for 30m.

marta-ops: Filing follow-up ticket INF-6421 to: - audit split-horizon DNS for cross-region consistency - verify LB cert SAN coverage - publish runbook for customer peering checks + recommended route advertisement ranges.

devon-sre: @liam-net please follow up on changing routing policy and cert SAN plan. Also log note: TTLs observed were 300s but some caches kept old mapping for ~15m.

liam-net: Acked, will schedule infra change and post ETA in eng-network channel.

sara.support: Closing urgent escalation, keeping thread open for the follow-up ticket updates. :white_check_mark:
